subject: [PATCH v2 0/2] mm/memory: refuse to map page cache folios that are not uptodate

reviews.author: Pedro Falcato
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Pedro Falcato suggested replacing a WARN_ON_ONCE() condition with an unlikely() macro, which would have the same effect as wrapping every call to the condition

Reviewer Pedro Falcato noted that the phrase 'read it in again' is too prescriptive, but otherwise approved the patch and gave a Reviewed-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
FYI you can wrap this line in an unlikely() and it has the same effect as
wrapping every call:
	return unlikely(!folio_test_anon(folio) && folio->mapping);

---

The "read it in again" sounds a bit too prescriptive but, apart from that:

Reviewed-by: Pedro Falcato <pfalcato@suse.de>

Thanks!

-- 
Pedro

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary:
Author prefers the retry logic to be placed closer to the fault handling code, specifically in __do_fault(), so that it's clear where the retry path is taken.

Author agreed to drop the WARN_ON_ONCE() in __do_fault() if a respin is required, and asked reviewer David to adjust the patch on application.
reviews.raw_body:
I prefer it at the call site. That is where the reader needs to see
that the retry is the rare path.

---

Okay, will drop it if respin needed.

David, could you adjust it on apply otherwise?

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Lorenzo pointed out that the patch's assumption about drivers returning page cache folios from ->fault() is incorrect, as some drivers like DAX set folio->mapping but don't reach the test. He suggested using 'rmappable' instead of 'page cache' and explicitly mentioning that ->fault might return non-rmappable folios.

Reviewer Lorenzo pointed out that folio_test_anon() can never return true in this context and suggested replacing the WARN_ON_ONCE() call with a VM_WARN_ON_ONCE() to simplify the code

Reviewer Lorenzo suggested removing an unlikely() condition in __do_fault(), as the true return case is already implicitly unlikely.
reviews.raw_body:
I guess you mean drivers that return non-page cache folios from ->fault()?
Because the driver could return page cache folios there (e.g. shmem), in
which case folio->mapping would be set (set on being added to the page
cache).

But also things are complicated by DAX (of course) which _does_ set
folio->mapping but installs the folio itself so won't reach the test
anyway.

So I think 'rmappable' is the better thing to say given DAX and, given this
is fiddly, maybe worth explicitly pointing out that ->fault might return
non-rmappable folios, e.g.:

	/*
	 * Drivers which specify ->fault() might return non-rmappable folios
	 * (in which case no PG_uptodate).
	 */

---

Technically folio_test_anon() can never return true based on where this is
called from right? Could this just be a:

	VM_WARN_ON_ONCE(folio_test_anon(folio));
	/* ... comment */
	return folio->mapping;

Instead?

(Note that __folio_add_file_rmap() asserts on folio_test_anon(folio)).

---

As Pedro said, I think this unlikely() is probably unnecessary given the true
return case is implicitly unlikely.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary:
The author addressed a concern that the folio lock might be dropped around ->page_mkwrite(), but pointed out this change occurred in 2007 and is not relevant to the current patch.

Author acknowledged that driver memory not in page cache can also return from ->fault(), but prefers to avoid using 'rmappable' due to its implications and accuracy issues, instead opting for the more accurate term 'page cache'.

Author acknowledged that all callers pass a file folio, agreed to add an assert at the top of the helper to check every call, including the rare uptodate case.

Author responds to feedback about where to place a retry in the code, initially preferring it at the call site but agreeing to move it if reviewer insists.
reviews.raw_body:
The window is from 2007, when __do_fault() started to drop the folio
lock around ->page_mkwrite():

Fixes: 6967614761fd ("ocfs2: release page lock before calling ->page_mkwrite")

Not sure how useful such Fixes is. It predates any possible stable tree.

---

Yes. How about:

        /*
         * ->fault() can also return driver memory that is not in the page
         * cache. It never gets PG_uptodate.
         */

I would rather avoid "rmappable". These folios do get
folio_add_file_rmap_ptes() in set_pte_range(), and the word reads like
PG_large_rmappable. As you said, DAX never reaches the check, so "page
cache" is accurate.

---

Right, all callers pass a file folio.

I will make it an assert, but at the top of the helper, so it checks
every call and not only the rare !uptodate one.

---

As I told Pedro, I prefer it at the call site. That is where the reader
needs to see that the retry is the rare path. But if you insist...

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lorenzo raised a concern about making an assumption based on where the `file_folio_not_uptodate` function is called from, suggesting that someone else could use it elsewhere and potentially bypass the check.
reviews.raw_body:
OK, though my concern is you're making an assumption based on where this is
called from, somebody else could use the function somewhere else and... :)

But this is nitpicking really, that's fine!

reviews.author: Matthew Wilcox
reviews.summary: Reviewer Matthew Wilcox argued that the patch is working around a bug in filesystems instead of fixing it directly, and requested that these issues be addressed
reviews.raw_body:
Filesystems that do this are buggy.  They shuld be fixed, not worked
around like this.

2026-11-09.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a problem where page cache folios that are not up-to-date can be mapped, leading to stale memory being leaked to userspace. The patches add a backstop to refuse mapping such folios in the __do_fault() and do_set_pmd() functions. Patch 1 fixes a race condition that would trip over this backstop by rechecking PG_uptodate after ->page_mkwrite().

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that filesystem fixes are needed before mm can map uptodate folios, suggests using WARN_ON_ONCE() and SIGBUS to flag buggy filesystems in the meantime.
reviews.raw_body:
Fair. What is your take on the way out?

Is there a timeline for the filesystem fixes?

Until they land, mm should still not map a folio that is not uptodate.

Would WARN_ON_ONCE() and SIGBUS, like the other checks in 2/2, work for
you? It flags the buggy filesystem instead of hiding it.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Matthew Wilcox
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that a filesystem marking a mapped folio as !uptodate will trigger other VM assertions, and suggested ignoring the bot's warning due to its limited knowledge.
reviews.raw_body:
It doesn't matter which way round the race ends up; if a filesystem marks
a mapped folio as !uptodate, there are other VM assertions that will
trip eventually.  This is one of those cases where we should ignore the
bot because it doesn't quite know enough.

2026-11-10.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a problem where page cache folios that are not up-to-date can be mapped, leading to stale memory being leaked to userspace. The patches add a backstop to refuse mapping such folios in the __do_fault() and do_set_pmd() functions. Patch 1 fixes a race condition that would trip over this backstop by rechecking PG_uptodate after ->page_mkwrite().
